question: Consider the following Statement-I : In the extraction of Al by Hall-Heroult process, pure $\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3$ mixed with $\mathrm{Na}_3\mathrm{Al}/\mathrm{F}_6$ lowers its melting point and increases conductivity. Statement-II : Zirconium metal is purified by zone refining method. The correct answer is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S1]

options.A: Both statement-I and statement-II are correct
options.B: Both statement-I and statement-II are not correct
options.C: Statement-I is correct, but statement-II is not correct
options.D: Statement-I is not correct, but statement-II is  correct

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Statement I In the extraction of Al by the Hall-Héroult process, pure $\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3$ mixed with $\mathrm{Na}_3\mathrm{AlF}_6$ lowers its melting point and increases conductivity. True. In the Hall-Héroult process, pure alumina $(\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3)$ has a very high melting point $(\sim 2050^{\circ}\mathrm{C})$ . It is dissolved in molten cryolite ( $\mathrm{Na}_3\mathrm{AlF}_6$ ) and sometimes small quantities of $\mathrm{CaF}_2$ are also added. The cryolite mixture lowers the melting point to around $950-1000^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and increases the electrical conductivity of the electrolyte. Hence, Statement I is correct. Statement II Zirconium metal is purified by zone refining method. Incorrect. The zone refining method is used for metals that need to be extremely pure and are less reactive, such as silicon, germanium, gallium, indium, etc. Zirconium (and hafnium) are purified by the van Arkel (iodide) process, not by zone refining. This process involves conversion of crude Zr into volatile $\mathrm{ZrI}_4$ , which then decomposes on a hot filament to yield pure zirconium metal. Hence, Statement II is not correct. © examsnet.com

question: $\lfloor t \rfloor$ denotes the greatest integer function and $\lfloor t - m \rfloor = \lfloor t \rfloor - m$ when $m \in \mathbb{Z}$ . solution: Solution: $\because \lfloor 2x - 2 \rfloor = \lfloor (2x - 1) - 1 \rfloor$ $= \lfloor 2x - 1 \rfloor - 1$ $\text{ let, } \lfloor 2x - 1 \rfloor = a$ $\Rightarrow \lfloor 2x - 2 \rfloor = a - 1$ $\text{ so, } 3(a-1) + 1 = 2a - 1$ $\Rightarrow 3a - 3 + 1 = 2a - 1 \Rightarrow a = 1$ thus $\lfloor 2x - 1 \rfloor = 1$ $\Rightarrow 1 \leq (2x - 1) < 2 \Rightarrow 2 \leq 2x < 3$ $\Rightarrow 1 \leq x < 1.5$ so, $x \in [1, 1.5)$ Now, $k = 2\lfloor 2x - 1 \rfloor - 1 = 2(1) - 1 = 1$ for $x \in [1, 1.5)$ $f(x) = \lfloor k + 5x \rfloor = \lfloor 1 + 5x \rfloor$ $\text{ at } x=1, f(x) = \lfloor 6 \rfloor = 6 \quad (\text{ minimum })$ $\text{ at } x=1.5, f(x) = \lfloor 1 + 5 \times 1.5 \rfloor$ $= \lfloor 8.5 \rfloor = 8 \quad \text{ (maximum) }$ so, $f(x)$ can be $6, 7, 8$ Hence, the range of $f(x)=\{6,7,8\}$ © examsnet.com

question: If $z$ is a complex number such that $\;\frac{z-1}{z-i}$ is purely imaginary and locus of $z$ represents a circle with centre ( $\alpha, \beta$ ) and radius $r$ ; then $\;\frac{\alpha}{\beta}+\;\frac{\beta}{\alpha}=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $\; \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}+i}{\sqrt{3}-i}\right)^{n}=-1$ $\; \because\; \text{ Modulus of numerator }\;=\sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^{2}+1^{2}}$ $\;=2\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}$ and modulus of denominator $=2$ $\;\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)=-\frac{\pi}{6}$ $\; \therefore \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}+i}{\sqrt{3}-i}\right)^{n} = \left(\frac{2\text{cis}\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)}{2\text{cis}\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)}\right)^{n}$ $\;= \left[\text{cis}\left(\frac{\pi}{6}-\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)\right]^{n}$ $\;= \left[\text{cis}\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right]^{n}=\text{cis}\left(\frac{n\pi}{3}\right)$ and $\text{cis}\left(\frac{n\pi}{3}\right) =-1$ $\;=\text{cis}(\pi)$ $\; \therefore \;\; \frac{n\pi}{3}=\pi$ $\; \Rightarrow \;\; n=3$ thus, $p=3$ Similarly, second expression $\; \left(\frac{1-\sqrt{3}i}{1+\sqrt{3}i}\right)^{m}=\text{cis}\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)$ $\Rightarrow \left[\frac{2\left(\text{cis}\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right)}{2\left(\text{cis}\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right)}\right]^{m}=\text{cis}\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)$ $\Rightarrow \left[\text{cis}\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right]^{m}=\text{cis}\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)$ $\Rightarrow \text{cis}\left(-\frac{2\pi}{3}\cdot m\right)=\text{cis}\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)$ Therefore, $-\frac{2\pi}{3}\cdot m=\frac{2\pi}{3}$ $\Rightarrow -2\pi m \equiv 2\pi \cdot \bmod(6\pi)$ $\Rightarrow -2m \equiv 2 \bmod(6)$ $\Rightarrow 2m \equiv -2 \equiv 4 \bmod 6$ $\Rightarrow m=2 \bmod 3$ ∴ Least positive integer $=m=2$ thus, $q=2$ Hence, $\sqrt{q^{2}+p^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}+2^{2}}=\sqrt{13}$ © examsnet.com

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Let, $a = x \hat{i} + y \hat{j} + z \hat{k}$ then, $a \times i = \widehat{\begin{vmatrix} i & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ x & y & z \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \end{vmatrix}}$ $= \hat{i}(0-0) - \hat{j}(0-z) + \hat{k}(0-y)$ $= z \hat{j} - y \hat{k}$ So, $\left| a \times i \right|^2 = z^2 + y^2$ Similarly, $\left| a \times \hat{j} \right|^2 = x^2 + z^2$ and $\left| a \times \hat{k} \right|^2 = x^2 + y^2$ thus, $\left| a \times \hat{i} \right|^2+\left| a \times \hat{j} \right|^2+\left| a \times \hat{k} \right|^2$ $= 2 (x^2 + y^2 + z^2)$ $\because a$ is unit vector So, $x^2+y^2+z^2=1$ Hence, $\left| a \times \hat{i} \right|^2+\left| a \times \hat{j} \right|^2+\left| a \times \hat{k} \right|^2$ $= 2 \times 1 = 2$ © examsnet.com

question: $3 \overline{i}+\overline{j}+\overline{k}, 2 \overline{i}+\overline{k}, \overline{i}+5 \overline{j}$ are the position vectors of three non collinear points $A, B, C$ respectively. If the perpendicular drawn from C onto $\overline{AB}$ meets $\overline{AB}$ at the point $a \overline{i}+b \overline{j}+c \overline{k}$ , then $a+b+c=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $AB = OB - OA = (2-3)\hat{i}+(0-1)\hat{j}+(1-1)\hat{k} = -\hat{i}-\hat{j}$ So, the direction vector of $\text{lin} E A B$ is $d = -\hat{i} - \hat{j}$ $\text{let} P = A + \lambda d$ $= (3\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}) + \lambda(-\hat{i}-\hat{j})$ $= (3-\lambda)\hat{i} + (1-\lambda)\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $PC = C - P = (\hat{i} + 5\hat{j})$ $-[(3-\lambda)\hat{i} + (1-\lambda)\hat{j} + \hat{k})$ $= (\lambda-2)\hat{i} + (4+\lambda)\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ As, given in the question $\because PC \perp AB$ $\Rightarrow PC \cdot AB = 0$ $\Rightarrow (\lambda-2)(-1) + (4+\lambda)(-1) + (-1)(0) = 0$ $\Rightarrow -\lambda+2-4-\lambda = 0$ $\Rightarrow \lambda = -1$ $\therefore P = (3-\lambda)\hat{i} + (1-\lambda)\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ $= (3+1)\hat{i} + (1+1)\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ $= 4\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ therefore, $a=4, b=2$ and $c=1$ Hence, $a+b+c=4+2+1=7$ © examsnet.com

question: Let $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{11}$ be the observations satisfying $\sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} (x_i-4)=22$ and $\sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} (x_i-4)^2=154$ . If the mean and variance of the observations are $\alpha$ and $\beta$ , then the quadratic equation having the roots $\;\frac{\alpha}{\beta}$ and $\;\frac{\beta}{\alpha}$ is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $\;\sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} (x_i-4)=22$ $\;\Rightarrow \;\; \sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} x_i - 4 \times 11 = 22$ $\;\Rightarrow \;\; \sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} x_i = 66$ So, mean $(\overline{x}) = \frac{66}{11} = 6$ and $\sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} (x_i-4)^2 = 154$ $\because \;\; x_i - \overline{x} = x_i - 6$ $= (x_i-4) - 2$ $\therefore \;\; [x_i - \overline{x}]^2 = [ (x_i-4) - 2 ]^2$ $= (x_i-4)^2 - 4(x_i-4) + 4$ So, $\sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} (x_i-\overline{x})^2 = \sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} (x-4)^2$ $-4 \sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} (x_i-4) + 11 \times 4$ $= 154 - 4 \times 22 + 44 = 110$ $\;\text{Variance}\; (\sigma) = \frac{1}{n} \sum (x_i-\overline{x})^2 \\ = \frac{1}{11} \times 110 = 10$ Thus, $\alpha = 6, \beta = 10$ Therefore, $\;\frac{\alpha}{\beta} + \;\frac{\beta}{\alpha} = \;\frac{6}{10} + \;\frac{10}{6} = \;\frac{3}{5} + \;\frac{5}{3}$ $= \frac{9+25}{15} = \frac{34}{15} = \;\text{Sum of roots}\;$ and $\;\frac{\alpha}{\beta} \cdot \;\frac{\beta}{\alpha} = 1 =$ product of roots Hence, the quadratic is $\;x^2 - \left(\;\frac{34}{15}\right) x + 1 = 0$ $\Rightarrow 15x^2 - 34x + 15 = 0$ © examsnet.com

question: A die is thrown twice. Let A be the event of getting a prime number when the die is thrown first time and $B$ be the event of getting an even number when the die is thrown second time. Then $P(A / \overline{B})$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Total outcomes $=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}=6$ Prime number $=\{2,3,5\}=3$ So, $P(A)=\frac{3}{6}=\frac{1}{2}$ and even numbers $=\{2,4,6\}=3$ $\therefore P(B)=\frac{3}{6}=\frac{1}{2}$ Thus, $P(\overline{B})=1-P(B)=1-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}$ Total sample for 2 throws $=6 \times 6=36$ Then, $P(A / \overline{B})=\frac{P(A \cap \overline{B})}{P(\overline{B})}$ First throw is prime $=\{2,3,5\}$ Second throw is not even $=\{1,3,5\}$ Pairs where first is in $\{2,3,5\}$ and second is in $\{1,3,5\}=3 \times 3=9$ outcomes So, $P(A \cap \overline{B})=\frac{9}{36}=\frac{1}{4}$ Therefore, $P(A / \overline{B})=\frac{\frac{1}{4}}{\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{1}{2}$ © examsnet.com

question: A bag contains 5 balls of unknown colours. There are equal chances that out of these five balls, there may be 0 or 1 or 2 or 3 or 4 or 5 red balls. A ball is taken out from the bag at random and is found to be red. The probability that it is the only red ball in the bag is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Let $R_k$ be the event that are exactly $k$ red balls is in bag, where $k=1,2,3,4,5$ So, $P(R_k) = \frac{1}{5}$ for $k=1,2,3,4,5$ Let $A$ be the event that a red ball is drawn. $P(R_1 / A) = \frac{P(R_1 \cap A)}{P(A)}$ $\because\ P(A / R_1) = \frac{1}{5}$ $\text{ and }\ P(R_1 \cap A) = P(R_1) \cdot P(A / R_1)$ $= \frac{1}{5} \cdot \frac{1}{5} = \frac{1}{25}$ $\text{ and }\ P(A) = \sum\limits_{k=0}^{5} P(R_k) \cdot P(A / R_k)$ $= \frac{1}{5} \sum\limits_{k=0}^{5} \frac{k}{5} = \frac{1}{25}(1+2+3+4+5)$ $= \frac{1}{25} \times 15 = \frac{15}{25}$ Hence, $P(R_1 / A) = \frac{P(R_1 \cap A)}{P(A)} = \frac{\frac{1}{25}}{\frac{15}{25}} = \frac{1}{15}$ © examsnet.com

question: The mean and variance of a binomial distribution are x and 5 respectively. If x is an integer, then the possible values for x are [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: The mean of a binomial distribution is $x$ , and the variance is 5 . We know that the mean, $\mu = n p = x$ . This means $n$ times $p$ is $x$ . The formula for variance is $\sigma^2 = n p (1-p) = 5$ . This means $n$ times $p$ times $(1-p)$ is 5 . From the mean formula, $p = \frac{x}{n}$ . Substitute $p = \frac{x}{n}$ into the variance formula: $x \left(1 - \frac{x}{n}\right) = 5$ If we open the bracket, we get: $x - \frac{x^2}{n} = 5$ Take $\frac{x^2}{n}$ to the other side: $\frac{x^2}{n} = x - 5$ Now, solve for $n$ : $n = \frac{x^2}{x-5}$ To get a whole number for $n, x-5$ must divide $x^2$ exactly. Let's check different $x$ values: If $x=6: n = \frac{36}{1} = 3636$ is an integer. If $x=10: n = \frac{100}{5} = 2020$ is an integer. If $x=30: n = \frac{900}{25} = 3636$ is an integer. So, the possible values for $x$ are: $6,10,30$ . © examsnet.com

question: After the coordinate axes are rotated through an angle $\;\frac{\pi}{4}$ in the anti clockwise direction without shifting the origin, if the equation $x^2+y^2-2x-4y-20=0$ transforms to $ax^2+2hxy+by^2+2gx+2fy+c=0$ in the new coordinate system, then $\begin{vmatrix} a & h & g \\ h & b & f \\ g & f & c \end{vmatrix}=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $\because x^2+y^2-2x-4y-20=0$ After rotation of axes through $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$ , it transforms to $ax^2+2hxy+by^2+2gx+2fy+c=0$ in the given equation $a=1, h=0, b=1, g=-1, f=-2, c=-20$ After rotation of $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$ $a' = a\cos^2\theta + b\sin^2\theta + 2h\cos\theta\sin\theta$ $\;\;\; = 1\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 + 1\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 + 0 = 1$ $b' = a\sin^2\theta + b\cos^2\theta - 2h\sin\theta\cos\theta$ $\; = 1\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 + 1\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 - 0 = 1$ also, $h' = (b-a)\sin\theta\cos\theta + h(\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta)$ $\; = 0+0 = 0$ Similarly, $x' = x\cos\theta - y\sin\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(x-y)$ and $y' = x\sin\theta + y\sin\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(x+y)$ then ${-2x'-4y'} = \frac{-2x+2y-4x-4y}{\sqrt{2}}$ $\; = \frac{-6x-2y}{\sqrt{2}}$ $\; = -3\sqrt{2}x - \sqrt{2}y = 2gx + 2fy$ then $g = -\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}, f = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, c = -20$ So, $\;\begin{vmatrix} a & h & g \\ h & b & f \\ g & f & c \end{vmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 & -\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -20 \end{vmatrix}$ $\;\;\; = 1\left(-20-\frac{1}{2}\right) - \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}\left(+\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$ $\;\;\; = -\frac{41}{2} - \frac{9}{2} = -25$ © examsnet.com

question: $A(-2,3)$ is a point on the line $4x+3y-1=0$ . If the points on the line that are 10 units away from the point $A$ are $(x_1, y_1)$ and $(x_2, y_2)$ , then $(x_1+y_1)^2+(x_2+y_2)^2=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $\;4x+3y-1=0$ $\;\;\text{Normal vector}\;=\langle 4,3\rangle$ Direction vectors are perpendicular to the normal vector $d=\langle 3,-4\rangle\;\text{or}\;\langle-3,4\rangle$ Unit vector in direction vector $\;=\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{3^2+(-4)^2}}\langle 3,-4\rangle$ $\;=\;\frac{1}{5}\langle 3,-4\rangle$ So, two points 10 units away from $A=(-2,3)$ along the line are $\; (x_1, y_1)=(-2,3)+10\cdot\frac{1}{5}\langle 3,-4\rangle$ $\;=(-2+6,3-8)=(4,-5)$ $\;\;\text{and}\; (x_2, y_2)=(-2,3)-10\cdot\frac{1}{5}\langle 3,-4)$ $\;=(-2-6,3+8)$ $\;=(-8,11)$ Therefore, $(x_1+y_1)^2+(x_2+y_2)^2$ $=(4-5)^2+(-8+11)^2$ $=1+9=10$ © examsnet.com

(i) $2 x^2+x y-y^2=0$ assume $y=m x$ , and substitute $2 x^2+x(m x)-(m x)^2=0$ Coefficient of $x^2$ should be zero $\Rightarrow \;\; 2+m-m^2=0 \Rightarrow m=2,-1$ $m_1=2 \;\text{ and }\; m_2=-1$ ∵ Both lines are perpendicular their slopes must be $-\;\frac{1}{m_1}=-\;\frac{1}{2} \;\text{ and }\; \frac{-1}{m_2}=1$ So, the perpendicular lines has their slopes $-\frac{1}{2}$ and 1 and passing through $(1,1)$ ∴ Pair of lines are $\; (y-y_1-m_1 (x-x_1) )$ $\; (y-y_1-m_2 (x-x_2) )=0$ $\Rightarrow \left(y-1+\frac{1}{9}(x-1)\right) (y-1-(x-1))=0$ $\Rightarrow \left(\frac{x}{2}+y-\frac{3}{2}\right) (y-x)=0$ $\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} x y-\frac{1}{2} x^2+y^2-x y-\frac{3}{2} y+\frac{3}{2} x=0$ $\Rightarrow -x^2-x y+2 y^2-3 y+3 x=0$ Compare with $\;\;\; a x^2+2 h x y+b y^2+2 g x+3 y=0$ $\; \therefore \;\; a=-1, h=+\frac{1}{2}, b=2 g=-\frac{3}{2}$ $\;\;\text{ so, }\; \frac{b}{a}=\frac{2}{-1}=-2$ $\;\;\text{ and }\; 2(g+h)=2 \left(-\frac{3}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\right) =-2$ Hence, $\frac{b}{a}=2(g+h)$ © examsnet.com

question: If the combined equation of the lines joining the origin to the points of intersection of the curve $x^2+y^2-2x-4y+2=0$ and the line $x+y-2=0$ is $(l_1x+m_1y)(l_2x+m_2y)=0$ , then $l_1+l_2+m_1+m_2=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Put $x=2-y$ in the given conic $\Rightarrow (2-y)^2+y^2-2(2-y)-4y+2=0$ $\Rightarrow y^2-4y+4+y^2-4+2y-4y+2=0$ $\Rightarrow 2y^2-6y+2=0 \Rightarrow y^2-3y+1$ $\therefore y=\frac{3\pm\sqrt{5}}{2}$ $\Rightarrow y_1=\frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2}, y_2=\frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}$ Thus, $x_1=2-\left(\frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2}\right)=\frac{1-\sqrt{5}}{2}$ and $x_2=2-\left(\frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}\right)=\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}$ then, $p_1 \equiv \left(\frac{1-\sqrt{5}}{2}, \frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2}\right)$ and $p_2 \equiv \left(\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}, \frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}\right)$ The lines $OP_1$ and $OP_2$ will have equation of the form $y=mx$ $\Rightarrow lx+my=0$ $\because m_1=\frac{y_1}{x_1}=\frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{1-\sqrt{5}}$ $=\frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{1-\sqrt{5}} \times \frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{1+\sqrt{5}} = -2-\sqrt{5}$ $\text{ and } m_2=\frac{y_2}{x_2}=\frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{1+\sqrt{5}}$ $=\frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{1+\sqrt{5}} \times \frac{1-\sqrt{5}}{1-\sqrt{5}} = -2+\sqrt{5}$ ∴ Combined equation of lines are $(m_1x-y_1)(m_2x-y)=0$ will form $\Rightarrow (l_1x+m_1y)(l_2x+m_2y)=0$ Lets expands and compare $m_1m_2x^2-(m_1+m_2)xy+y^2=l_1l_2x^2$ $+(l_1m_2+l_2m_1)xy+m_1m_2y^2$ $\therefore l_1l_2=m_1m_2, \quad l_1m_2+l_2m_1=-(m_1+m_2),$ $m_1m_2=1$ $m_1=-2-\sqrt{5}, \quad m_2=-2+\sqrt{5}$ $\text{ and } m_1+m_2=-4$ $\because l_1l_2=m_1m_2=1$ $\Rightarrow l_1=\frac{1}{l_2}$ $\therefore l_1m_2+\frac{m_1}{l_1}=4$ $\Rightarrow (\sqrt{5}-2)l_1^2+(-\sqrt{5}-2)=4l_1.$ $\Rightarrow l_1=1 \text{ and } l_2=1$ Hence, $l_1+l_2+m_1+m_2=1+1-4=-2$ © examsnet.com

question: The slope of one of the direct common tangents drawn to the circles $x^2+y^2-2x+4y+1=0$ and $x^2+y^2-4x-2y+4=0$ is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

solution: Solution: $\;c_1: x^2+y^2-2x+4y+1=0$ $\;\Rightarrow (x-1)^2+(y+2)^2=4$ Centre $(c_1) =(1,-2), r_1=2$ and $c_2: x^2+y^2-4x-2y+4=0$ $\Rightarrow (x-2)^2+(y-1)^2=1$ Centre $(c_2) =(2,1), r_2=1$ $c_1 c_2=d={\sqrt{(2-1)^2+ (1+2^2.}}={\sqrt{10}}$ Let the slope of direct common tangent be $m$ the general line is $y=mx+c$ this line has perpendicular distance $r_1$ from $c_1$ and $r_2$ from $c_2$ $\; \therefore \left| \frac{m(1)-(-2)+c}{\sqrt{1+m^2}} \right|=2$ $\;\Rightarrow |m+2+c|=2 \sqrt{1+m^2}$ $\;\; \text{ and } \left| \frac{m(2)-1+c}{\sqrt{1+m^2}} \right|=1$ $\;\Rightarrow |2m+c-1|=\sqrt{1+m^2}$ Put the value of ' $c$ ' from Eq. (i) to Eq. (ii) $2m-1+(-m-2+2\sqrt{m^2+1}) = \sqrt{m^2+1}$ $\Rightarrow m=3-\sqrt{m^2+1}$ Squaring both sides, we get $\;m^2=\;m^2+10$ $\Rightarrow \sqrt{m^2+1} -6\sqrt{m^2+1}$ $\Rightarrow\; m^2+1$ $\Rightarrow\; =\; \frac{25}{9}$ $\Rightarrow\; m^2=\frac{16}{9}$ $\Rightarrow\; m=\frac{4}{3}$ © examsnet.com

question: If (1, a), (b, 2) are conjugate points with respect to the circle $x^2+y^2=25$ , then $4 a+2 b=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: We are told that $(1, a)$ and $(b, 2)$ are conjugate points with respect to the circle $x^2+y^2=25$ . Step 1. Condition for conjugate points If $(x_1, y_1)$ and $(x_2, y_2)$ are conjugate points with respect to the circle $x^2+y^2=r^2$ , then the polar of one point passes through the other. Equation of the polar of $(x_1, y_1)$ w.r.t. $x^2+y^2=r^2$ is: $x_1 x+y_1 y=r^2$ Step 2. The point $(1, a)$ For the point $(1, a)$ , the polar is: $1 \cdot x+a \cdot y=25$ That is: $x+a y=25$ Step 3. The point $(b, 2)$ lies on this polar Since the points $(1, a)$ and $(b, 2)$ are conjugate, the point $(b, 2)$ lies on the polar of $(1, a)$ . So: $\;b+a(2)=25$ $\;b+2 a=25$ Step 4. Symmetry of conjugate points Similarly, the polar of $(b, 2)$ is: $b x+2 y=25$ And $(1, a)$ must lie on this polar: $b(1)+2(a)=25$ Wait-that would give same, yes so far matches (1). Let's check the other way: Substitute $(x, y)=(1, a)$ : $b \cdot 1+2 a=25$ This is the same as (1). So it's consistent. Step 5. We need $4 a+2 b=$ ? From (1): $b+2 a=25$ . Multiply both sides by 2 : $2 b+4 a=50$ So, $4 a+2 b=50 \; \text{". "} \;$ © examsnet.com

question: If the pole of the line $x+2by-5=0$ with respect to the circle $S \equiv x^2+y^2-4x-6y+4=0$ lies on the line $x+by+1=0$ , then the polar of the point ( $b, -b$ ) with respect to the circle $S=0$ is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

solution: Solution: Let $(h, k)$ be the pole of the line $x+2by-5=0$ with respect to the circle $\; s \equiv x^2+y^2-4x-6y+4=0$ $\; \therefore \; \; hx+ky-2(x+h)-3(y+k)+4=0$ $\; (h-2)x+(k-3)y-2h-3k+4=0$ is coincide with $x+2by-5=0$ $\; \frac{h-2}{1} \; = \; \frac{k-3}{2b} = \; \frac{2h+3k-4}{5}$ $\Rightarrow \; \frac{h-2}{1} \; = \; \frac{k-3}{2b}$ $2bh - k = 4b - 3 \; \; \; \cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot (i)$ and $\; \frac{h-2}{1} = \; \frac{2h+3k-4}{5}$ $h-k=2 \; \; \; \cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot (ii)$ Solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $h = \; \frac{4b-5}{2b-1}, \; k = \; \frac{-3}{2b-1}$ © examsnet.com

question: If $P(\alpha, \beta)$ is the radical centre of the circles $S \equiv x^2 + y^2 + 4x + 7 = 0$ , $S' \equiv 2x^2 + 2y^2 + 3x + 5y + 9 = 0$ and $S'' \equiv x^2 + y^2 + y = 0$ , then the length of the tangent drawn from P to $S' = 0$ is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: The given equations are $s: x^2 + y^2 + 4x + 7 = 0$ $s': 2x^2 + 2y^2 + 3x + 5y + 9 = 0$ $\Rightarrow x^2 + y^2 + \frac{3}{2}x + \frac{5}{2}y + \frac{9}{2} = 0$ $s'': x^2 + y^2 + y = 0$ Radical axis of $s$ and $s': s - s' = 0$ $\Rightarrow 4x - \frac{3}{2}x - \frac{5}{2}y + 7 - \frac{9}{2} = 0$ $\Rightarrow \frac{5}{2}x - \frac{5}{2}y + \frac{5}{2} = 0$ $\Rightarrow x - y + 1 = 0 \cdots (i)$ Radical axis of $s$ and $s'': s - s'' = 0$ $\Rightarrow 4x - y + 7 = 0 \cdots (ii)$ From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we have $x = -2, y = -1$ ∴ Radical centre is $P(-2, -1)$ Length of tangent from $P$ to $s'$ $= \sqrt{(-2)^2 + (-1)^2 + \frac{3}{2}(-2) + \frac{5}{2}(-1) + \frac{9}{2}}$ $= \sqrt{4 + 1 - 3 + 2} = \sqrt{4} = 2$ © examsnet.com

question: If the tangents of the parabola $y^2=8 x$ passing through the point $P(1,3)$ touches the parabola at $A$ and $B$ , then the area (in sq. units) of $\triangle ABC$ is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $y^2=8 x, a=2$ Equation of tangent $y=mx+\frac{2}{m}$ $\text{ at }(1,3)$ $3=m+\frac{2}{m} \Rightarrow m^2-3m+2=0$ $\Rightarrow m=1,2$ So, equation of tangent (put point $(1,3)$ on $y=mc+c$ ) $y=x+c, y=2x+c$ $\Rightarrow y=x+2 y=2x+1$ to find coordinates of $A$ and $B$ , put the line on parabola. $(x+2)^2=8x \Rightarrow x^2-4x+4=0$ $\Rightarrow x=2,-2$ $\text{ at } x=2, y=\sqrt{8\times2}=4$ So, $A=(2,4)$ and $(2x+1)^2=8x$ $\Rightarrow 4x^2-4x+1=0$ $\Rightarrow x=\frac{1}{2},-\frac{1}{2}$ $\text{ at } x=\frac{1}{2}, y=2$ So, $B=\left(\frac{1}{2},2\right)$ Now, area of $\triangle PAB$ $A=\frac{1}{2}\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 \\ \frac{1}{2} & 2 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$ $=\left| \frac{1}{2} \left(1(4-2)-3\left(2-\frac{1}{2}\right)+1(4-2)\right) \right|..$ $=\left| \frac{1}{2} \left(2-\frac{9}{2}+2\right) \right|=\left| \frac{1}{2} \left(4-\frac{9}{2}\right) \right|$ $=\left| \frac{1}{2} \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) \right|=\frac{1}{4}$ © examsnet.com

question: The equation of the normal drawn at the point $(\sqrt{2}+1,-1)$ to the ellipse $x^2+2 y^2-2 x+8 y+5=0$ is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $S(x, y) \equiv x^2+2 y^2-2 x+8 y+5$ Thus, $\; \frac{\partial s}{\partial x}=2 x-2 \; \frac{\partial s}{\partial y}=4 y+8$ at $P \equiv (\sqrt{2}+1,-1)$ $2 x-2=2(\sqrt{2}+1)-2=2 \sqrt{2}$ and $4 y+8=-4+8=4$ So, $n = \langle 2 \sqrt{2}, 4 \rangle$ So, slope $= \; \frac{4}{2 \sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}$ Then, equation of normal (at $\sqrt{2}+1,-1$ ) $\; y-(-1)=\sqrt{2}(x-(\sqrt{2}+1))$ $\Rightarrow y+1=\sqrt{2} x-2-\sqrt{2}$ $\Rightarrow y-\sqrt{2} x+\sqrt{2}+3=0$ $\Rightarrow \sqrt{2} x-y-3-\sqrt{2}=0$ $\Rightarrow \sqrt{2} x-y=3+\sqrt{2}$ © examsnet.com

question: If $3x+2\sqrt{2}y+k=0$ is a normal to the hyperbola $4x^2-9y^2-36=0$ making positive intercepts on both the axes, then $k=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $4x^2-9y^2=36 \Rightarrow \frac{x^2}{9}-\frac{y^2}{4}=0$ So, $a^2=9, b^2=4$ Thus, equation of normal $\frac{9x}{x_1}+\frac{4y}{y_1}=(9+4)=13 \;\;\;\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot(i)$ and the given equation is $3x+2\sqrt{2}y+k=0$ $\Rightarrow \;\; 3x+2\sqrt{2}y=-k \;\;\;\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot(ii)$ ∵ Both equation are proportional Thus, $\frac{\frac{9}{x_1}}{3}=\frac{\frac{4}{y_1}}{2\sqrt{2}}=\frac{13}{-k}$ $\Rightarrow \;\; \frac{3}{x_1}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{y_1} \Rightarrow x_1=\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} y_1$ Put in equation of hyperbola $\frac{\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} y_1\right)^2}{9}-\frac{y^2}{4}=1 \Rightarrow y_1^2=4 \Rightarrow y_1= \pm 2$ at $y_1=2 \Rightarrow x_1=3\sqrt{2}$ and at $y_1=-2$ $\Rightarrow x_1=-3\sqrt{2}$ Also, $\frac{3}{x_1}=-\frac{13}{k} \Rightarrow -k=\frac{13}{3} \times 3\sqrt{2}=13\sqrt{2}$ Hence, $k=-13\sqrt{2}$ © examsnet.com

question: If a hyperbola has asymptotes $3x-4y-1=0$ and $4x-3y-6=0$ , then the transverse and conjugate axes of that hyperbola are [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Asymptotes are $\;3x-4y-1=0 \;\;\;\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot (i)$ $\;4x-3y-6=0 \;\;\;\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot (ii)$ By Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $x=3, y=2$ Now, the direction vectors of asymptotes for $3x-4y=1 \Rightarrow d_1=\langle 4,3 \rangle$ and for $4x-3y=6 \Rightarrow d_2=\langle 3,4 \rangle$ Thus, transverse and conjugate axis directions. $\;\;\frac{L_1}{\sqrt{a_1^2+b_1^2}} = \pm \;\frac{L_2}{\sqrt{a_2^2+b_2^2}}$ $\Rightarrow \;\frac{3x-4y-1}{\sqrt{3^2+(-4)^2}} = \pm \;\frac{4x-3y-6}{\sqrt{4^2+(-3)^2}}$ $\Rightarrow 3x-4y-1 = \pm 4x-3y-6$ $\;\text{ So, }\;\;3x-4y-1=4x-3y-6$ $\;\text{ or }\;\;3x-4y-1=-4x+3y+6$ $\Rightarrow x+y-5=0$ $\;\text{ or }\;\;7x-7y-7=0$ $\Rightarrow x+y-5=0 \;\text{ or }\; x-y-1=$ Hence, transverse and conjugate axis are $x+y=5, x-y=1$ © examsnet.com

solution: Solution: $\;A(0,1,2), B(2,-1,3), C(1,-3,1)$ $\; \because   \;\;  B A =\langle -2,2,-1 \rangle$ $\; \;\;  B C =\langle -1,-2,-2 \rangle$ $\; \because   \;\;  B A \cdot B C =(-2)(-1)+2(-2)$ $\; \;\; +(-1)(-2)=0$ So, $\triangle A B C$ is right angled at $B$ . ∴ Orthocenter $(H)$ is at point $B=(2,-1,3)$ and circumcenter $(O)= \left( \;\frac{0+1}{2}, \;\frac{-3+1}{2}, \;\frac{1+2}{2} \right) = \left( \;\frac{1}{2},-1, \;\frac{3}{2} \right)$ Hence, $O H\;=\sqrt{ \left(2-\;\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+(-1+1)^2+ \left(3-\;\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 }$ $\;=\sqrt{\;\frac{9}{4}+\;\frac{9}{4}}=\;\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}$ © examsnet.com

question: If the direction cosines of two lines satisfy the equations $l-2m+n=0$ , $lm+10mn-2nl=0$ and $\theta$ is the angle between the lines, then $\cos \theta =$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $\because l-2m+n=0 \Rightarrow l=2m-n$ Substitute in $lm+10mn-2nl=0$ $\;\Rightarrow (2m-n)m+100mn-2n(2m-n)=0$ $\;\Rightarrow 2m^2+5mn+2n^2=0$ $\;\Rightarrow m = \frac{-5n \pm 3n}{4} = \frac{-n}{2}, -2n$ If $m = \frac{-n}{2}, l = -2n$ Then, direction ratios of are $1 : m : n = -2n : \frac{n}{2} : n = -4 : -1 : 2$ and direction cosine are $(-4k)^2+(-k)^2+(2k)^2=1 \Rightarrow k = \frac{1}{\sqrt{21}}$ $= \left( \frac{-4}{\sqrt{21}}, \frac{-1}{\sqrt{21}}, \frac{2}{\sqrt{21}} \right)$ If $m = -2n$ , then $l = -5n$ and DR's are $l : m : n = -5 : -2 : 1$ and DC's are $(-5k)^2+(-2k)^2+k^2=1$ $\Rightarrow \;\; k = \frac{1}{\sqrt{30}} = \left( \frac{-5}{\sqrt{30}}, \frac{-2}{\sqrt{30}}, \frac{1}{\sqrt{30}} \right)$ Therefore angle between given lines are $\;\cos \theta = \left| l_1 l_2 + m_1 m_2 + n_1 n_2 \right|$ $\; = \left| \frac{-4}{\sqrt{21}} \times \left( \frac{-5}{\sqrt{30}} \right) + \left( \frac{-1}{\sqrt{21}} \right) \right|$ $\left( \frac{-2}{\sqrt{30}} \right) + \left( \frac{2}{\sqrt{21}} \right) \left( \frac{1}{\sqrt{30}} \right) .$ $\; = \frac{24}{\sqrt{630}} = \frac{24}{3\sqrt{70}}$ $\; = \frac{8}{\sqrt{70}}$ © examsnet.com

question: If a real valued function $f(x)=\begin{cases} (1+\sin x)^{\csc x} & -\frac{\pi}{2} < x < 0 \\ a & x=0 \\ \frac{e^{\frac{2}{x}}+e^{\frac{3}{x}}}{a e^{\frac{2}{x}}+b e^{\frac{3}{x}}} & 0 < x < \frac{\pi}{2} \end{cases}$ , is continuous at $x=0$ , then $ab=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $f(x)=\begin{cases} (1+\sin x)^{\cos x} & -\frac{\pi}{2} < x < 0 \\ a & x=0 \\ \frac{e^{\frac{2}{x}}+e^{\frac{3}{x}}}{a e^{\frac{2}{x}}+b e^{\frac{3}{2}}} & 0 < x < \frac{\pi}{2} \end{cases}$ So, $\lim\limits_{x \to 0^{-}} f(x) = \lim\limits_{x \to 0^{-}} (1+\sin x)^{\cos x}$ Let $y = (1+\sin x)^{\cos x}$ $\Rightarrow \ln y = \cos x \ln (1+\sin x)$ $= \frac{\ln (1+\sin x)}{\sin x} = 1$ $\Rightarrow y = e$ $\therefore \lim\limits_{x \to 0^{-}} (1+\sin x)^{\cos x} = e = a = f(0)$ $\text{ and } \lim\limits_{x \to 0^{+}} f(x) = \lim\limits_{x \to 0^{+}} \frac{e^{\frac{2}{x}}+e^{\frac{3}{x}}}{a e^{\frac{2}{x}}+b e^{\frac{3}{2}}}$ $= \lim\limits_{x \to 0^{+}} \frac{e^{\frac{3}{x}} \left(e^{-\frac{1}{x}}+1\right)}{e^{\frac{3}{x}} \left(e \cdot e^{-\frac{1}{x}}+b\right)} = \frac{1}{b}$ So, $e = \frac{1}{b} \Rightarrow b = \frac{1}{e}$ Hence, $a b = e \cdot \frac{1}{e} = 1$ © examsnet.com

question: $\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{(\csc x-\cot x)(e^{x}-e^{-x})}{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2+\cos x}}=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: $\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{(\csc x-\cot x)(e^{x}-e^{-x})}{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2+\cos x}}$ Convert, $\csc x$ and $\cot x$ into $\sin x$ and $e^{x}-e^{-x}=2\sinh x$ $\;=\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{ \left( \frac{2\sin^{2}\frac{x}{2}}{2\sin\frac{x}{2}\cos\frac{x}{2}} \cdot 2\sinh x \right) }{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2+\cos x}}$ $\;=\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{2\tan\frac{x}{2}\cdot\sinh x}{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2+\cos x}} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2+\cos x}}{\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2+\cos x}}$ $\;=\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{2\tan\frac{x}{2}\cdot\sinh x(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2+\cos x})}{1-\cos x}$ $\;=\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{2\tan\frac{x}{2}\cdot\sinh x(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2+\cos x})}{1-\cos x}$ $\;=\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{ \frac{2\sin\frac{x}{2}}{\cos\frac{x}{2}} \cdot \sinh x(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2+\cos x}) }{2\sin^{2}\frac{x}{2}}$ $\;=\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{ \sinh x(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2+\cos x}) }{\cos\frac{x}{2} \cdot \sin\frac{x}{2}}$ $\; \because x \to 0 \Rightarrow \cos\frac{x}{2} \to 1 \;\text{ and }\; \sin\frac{x}{2} \to \frac{x}{2}$ $\; \sinh x \to x$ $\;=\;\frac{x(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2+1})}{\frac{x}{2}} = 2(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{3})$ $=2(2\sqrt{3}) = 4\sqrt{3}$ © examsnet.com
